newsitem.title: UK: Wheat prices seen pressured in early 1997 - IGC.
newsitem.headline: Wheat prices seen pressured in early 1997 - IGC.

text.p: World wheat prices could come under pressure early in 1997 with the impact of expected higher crops in southern hemisphere producers Argentina and Australia, the International Grains Council (IGC) said on Thursday.
In its latest monthly report, the IGC estimated the 1996 Australian crop at 19.0 million tonnes, 2.0 million up on 1995, and Argentine output at 14.5 million tonnes, 5.8 million higher.
Argentina is expected to have a big crop to export but its wheat will not be available on the world market until January, said Bill de Maria, the IGC's assistant executive director.
"They haven't got extensive storage facilities so the pressure for them will be to sell into the export market," de Maria said.
Any impact on prices was likely to take effect in the first quarter of 1997.
"The southern hemisphere harvests, as they become available, will have a strong influence on prices," de Maria told Reuters.
"There is the possibility of price pressure later in the season."
